issues.title: vectorElemMinSize recursion is quadratic in vector nesting depth
issues.verdictReason: vectorElemMinSize (marshal.go:1125) calls isVectorVariableLengthType, whose TypeCustom/VectorType case (marshal.go ~1180) recurses to the bottom of the nesting at every level, then vectorElemMinSize itself recurses into vec.SubType, so total work is sum(1..d) = O(d^2) for a type nested d levels deep; a server-controlled nested vector type string can make d arbitrarily large.
issues.scopeReason: vectorElemMinSize and its recursive use of isVectorVariableLengthType are new code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: vectorElemMinSize is quadratic in nesting depth

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: At every level of its own recursion vectorElemMinSize calls the fully recursive isVectorVariableLengthType, and unmarshalVector re-runs the bound at each nested level, so a deeply nested server-supplied type (~1400 levels) can make the client burn CPU regardless of actual value size.

issues.title: MaxInt32 saturation branch in dimension-bound math is untested
issues.verdictReason: TestVectorElemMinSize (marshal_vector_test.go:803-816) nests vector<vector<float,3>,4> at most; no test drives vec.Dimensions*per close to or past math.MaxInt32 to exercise the `int64(vec.Dimensions) > (math.MaxInt32-size)/per` saturation branch at marshal.go:1136.
issues.scopeReason: The saturation arithmetic is new code added by this PR and ships without a test for its only nontrivial branch.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: MaxInt32 saturation branch in the bound arithmetic is untested

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: No test exercises the saturation arithmetic beyond an inner dimension of 4, so a wrap, off-by-one, or 32-bit narrowing bug in that branch would go undetected.

issues.title: Float fast-path length-mismatch check is no longer independently tested
issues.verdictReason: Verified: for the existing float64_unmarshal_wrong_data_len test (10 bytes, 3 dims) the new dimension bound (3 > 10/8) already rejects before the fast path's own len(data)!=expected check runs; a case like 28 bytes/3 dims passes the bound (3 > 28/8=3 is false) and would only be caught by the fast-path check, which no test drives.
issues.scopeReason: The new bound check shadows the pre-existing fast-path length check in the only tests that exercised it, created by this PR's change.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Float fast-path length-mismatch check is no longer exercised by tests

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: Existing wrong-length tests are now caught by the new bound first and only assert that some error occurred, so removing the fast-path len(data) != expected checks would still pass all tests (e.g. 28 bytes into *[]float64 with 3 dimensions would decode without error).

issues.title: PR body claims every new test fails on pristine code; several already pass
issues.verdictReason: Verified by running the test file against base marshal.go/helpers.go (main, with a no-op vectorElemMinSize stub so it compiles): TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads, TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType, and the 'nested vector into a concrete slice still decodes' / 'a resolvable element type into an interface still decodes' subtests all PASS unmodified, contradicting the PR body's claim that every new test fails against pristine code.
issues.scopeReason: The overstatement is in this PR's own description of its own verification.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: PR body overstates that every new test fails against pristine code

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: Several new tests (TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads, TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType, and two 'still decodes' subtests) assert behaviour the base code already has, contradicting the claim that every new test fails against pristine marshal.go/helpers.go.

issues.title: Bound's comment wrongly claims every path allocates
issues.verdictReason: In unmarshalVector's reflect.Array branch (marshal.go ~1053-1067), the code checks rv.Len() against info.Dimensions and writes directly into the existing array via rv.Index(i) with no make/reflect.MakeSlice call, so the comment's claim that 'every path below turns it into an allocation' is incorrect for that path.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new, added alongside the bound in this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Bound's comment inaccurately claims every path allocates

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: The comment says 'every path below turns it into an allocation', but the *[N]T array path allocates nothing, which the PR's own test comment acknowledges.

issues.title: Test comment misstates per-element byte size of nested text vector
issues.verdictReason: The payload is two inner vector<text,3> elements, each a 1-byte outer vint length prefix plus three 1-byte zero-length vints = 4 bytes per inner vector, totaling 8 bytes for both (matching the test's len(data)==8 assertion); the comment's 'eight bytes' describes the whole two-element payload, not one inner vector as its phrasing implies.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new test documentation added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Test comment states wrong byte size for inner vector

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: A comment says each inner vector<text,3> is 'eight bytes', but each one is actually 4 bytes; 8 is the size of the whole two-element payload.

issues.title: Test comment's 'N bytes' rationale doesn't name the real per-type bound
issues.verdictReason: The code's actual bound is info.Dimensions * vectorElemMinSize(SubType), which exceeds N bytes for any element type with a per-element minimum above 1 byte (e.g. 12 bytes for 3 floats, 48 for the nested-vector case in the same test); stating the floor as 'N bytes' describes a weaker, type-blind invariant rather than the bound the tests are actually pinned against.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new test documentation added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Stale rationale in test doc comment about minimum vector encoding size

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: The comment argues 'a vector of N elements is never encoded in fewer than N bytes', but the actual bound is Dimensions * vectorElemMinSize, not N bytes.

issues.title: makeVectorType duplicates makeFloat32VectorType/makeDoubleVectorType
issues.verdictReason: makeVectorType(TypeFloat, "FloatType", dim) and makeVectorType(TypeDouble, "DoubleType", dim) build byte-for-byte the same VectorType as makeFloat32VectorType(dim) and makeDoubleVectorType(dim) (marshal_vector_test.go:36-61), and the new tests use both builder styles interchangeably.
issues.scopeReason: makeVectorType is a new test helper added by this PR alongside the pre-existing, now-duplicated ones.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: makeVectorType duplicates existing test helper functions

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/tidepool/review: makeVectorType duplicates what makeFloat32VectorType and makeDoubleVectorType already build, and the new tests mix both styles, meaning a change to the vector type's layout or name format must be repeated across multiple builders.

issues.title: Commit message not naming vectorElemMinSize is not a defect
issues.verdictReason: Commit 0276a66's message already explains the mechanism in plain terms ('Every element takes at least one byte on the wire, so a count the buffer cannot hold is rejected'); omitting the internal helper function's name is not an inaccuracy or missing requirement.
issues.scopeReason: Concerns this PR's own commit message, but asserts no actual inaccuracy.
